recover.ownership: Use this only on archives you own or have permission to open. Recovering someone else’s password may be illegal.
recover.expectations: Finding a password can take anywhere from seconds to days — and may not succeed at all — depending on how long and complex it is. This is not a magic tool: short, numeric, or common passwords are found quickly, but long random ones can be impractical.
recover.toolsHint: This feature runs three open-source tools as separate programs. They are not bundled; add them with the automatic download (checksum-verified where the source publishes one) or manually.
recover.purpose.known-plaintext: Fastest, if you have a known file
recover.consentText: Download {name} ({size} MB, {license} license) from its official source?
recover.consentAgree: I understand this downloads a third-party tool from its official source.
recover.checksumMismatch: The download did not match the published checksum and was discarded. Try again or use the manual download.
recover.setupIntro: This feature needs three free, open-source tools. Quick Extract Ultra does not include them, so choose how to add them. You only do this once; they stay on your PC.
recover.autoRiskNote: Automatic download fetches the latest version of each tool from its official source over HTTPS. bkcrack is also checksum-verified; hashcat and John are downloaded from their official sites, which publish a PGP signature rather than a checksum the app can auto-check. You can verify any file later from the tools folder.
recover.setupFailed: Could not add: {names}. Use the manual button for those.
recover.infoWhy: Recovering a ZIP password is heavy computation done by specialized programs. Quick Extract Ultra contains none of that code — it runs three trusted open-source tools as separate programs. They are not bundled so the app stays small, so their licenses (one is GPL) stay separate, and so you choose exactly what runs on your PC.
recover.infoSafety: Automatic download always fetches from each tool’s official website or GitHub release over HTTPS, so it is the safest option. If you download manually, use only the official pages listed below, check that the file name matches the current version, and do not run a copy from any other website — a fake build could contain malware. When a source publishes a signature or checksum, you can verify the file yourself.
recover.infoAutoNote: Downloaded tools are kept in your tools folder; nothing is uploaded, and the app never re-hosts these files. Note: Windows Defender or antivirus may flag these tools as "hacktools" and remove them; if a tool disappears or will not run, allow it in your antivirus.
recover.notZip: This feature works with ZIP and RAR files only. "{name}" is a {type} file.
recover.zipOnly: ZIP and RAR files (other formats are not supported here).
recover.rarSlow: This is a RAR file. RAR uses strong encryption, so recovery is much slower than ZIP — realistically only short, numeric, or common passwords can be found.
recover.knownHint: This ZIP uses legacy ZipCrypto. If you still have one original (unencrypted) file that is inside it, bkcrack can recover it very fast.
recover.autoPitch: Recommended. The app tries the most effective methods in order: common passwords with variations, then number-only passwords (PINs, dates), then a smart search that tries the most likely passwords first. No settings needed — just press the button. Use the other tabs only if you want to narrow the search yourself.
recover.bruteWarn: Brute force gets much slower with each extra character. Try a wordlist first.
recover.powerHint: Balanced uses about half your CPU so the machine does not overheat. Economy runs cooler and quieter; Maximum is fastest but runs the machine hard.
recover.needTool: Add at least one tool above (John works on any PC; hashcat needs a GPU).

recover.stage.john: Searching on the CPU with John...
recover.keysFoundLabel: Keys recovered. The files can be extracted now.
